predecessors.name: Wei (Warring States)
predecessors.text: the Zhongshan core, which Wei held after conquering it in 407: 'in 381, Zhongshan won its independence back'

predecessors.name: Xianyu
predecessors.text: 'Zhongshan occupies roughly the same place as the earlier Xianyu state'

successors.name: Zhao (Warring States)
successors.text: the Zhongshan core that the Zhongshan page names (Lingshou, Dongyuan, the Baoding wall); the same disc set as the wei and zhao dossiers

capitals.name: Lingshou (靈壽), ruins in Pingshan County, Hebei

ledger.x: 381: Zhongshan wins its independence back from Wei.
296: Zhao annexes the rest of Zhongshan.

wars.name: Wei conquest of Zhongshan
wars.outcome: Wei troops conquered Zhongshan in 407 ('Soon after this, in 407, Zhongshan was conquered by Wei troops'); Marquess Wen gave the land to his eldest son Ji; in 381 'Zhongshan won its independence back'.

wars.name: Zhongshan invasion of Yan
wars.outcome: 'Zhongshan invaded Yan in 315', after Yan's king abdicated; Zhongshan seized copper mines and Qi joined the war.

wars.name: Zhao's conquest of Zhongshan
wars.outcome: Zhao victory: attacks 'almost every year' from 307, several cities in 307, parts annexed in 305, the king took refuge in Qi in 301, the state annexed in 296 (295 on the Zhao page).
